label: USB devices
pick_label: A USB device or external drive is not recognized

u_start.text: Is the device that isn't working a storage drive (flash drive or external hard drive), or something else?
u_start.why: Storage drives have extra checks, such as Windows seeing the drive but not giving it a drive letter.

options.label: Flash drive or external hard drive

u_port.title: Try a different USB port and cable
u_port.do: Unplug the drive and plug it straight into a different USB port on the computer. Avoid USB hubs and front-panel extension cables. If the drive has its own cable, try another one.
u_port.why: Single ports, hubs and cables fail on their own, and a weak connection is the most common reason a drive does not show up.
u_port.expect: Windows plays a sound and the drive appears in File Explorer within a few seconds.

u_done_port.cause: A faulty USB port, hub or cable.
u_done_port.learn: A USB port supplies both data and power. If either connection is poor, the device may not be detected at all, even though it looks plugged in.

u_port_o.title: Try a different USB port and cable
u_port_o.do: Unplug the device and plug it straight into a different USB port on the computer. Avoid USB hubs and extension cables. If the device has its own cable, try another one.
u_port_o.why: Single ports, hubs and cables fail on their own, so changing one at a time shows which part is the problem.
u_port_o.expect: Windows plays a sound and the device is set up within a few seconds.

u_done_port_o.cause: A faulty USB port, hub or cable.
u_done_port_o.learn: A USB port supplies both data and power. If either connection is poor, the device may not be detected at all, even though it looks plugged in.

u_test.text: Plug the same device into another computer. Does it work there?
u_test.why: If it fails on another computer too, the device or its cable is the likely problem and not this computer.

options.label: Yes, it works on the other computer

u_disk.caution: Do not format the drive or delete a partition here. That erases everything on it.
u_disk.title: Check whether Windows can see the drive
u_disk.do: Right-click the Start button and open Disk Management. Look in the lower list for your drive. If it appears with no drive letter, right-click its partition, choose 'Change Drive Letter and Paths', and click Add. Do NOT choose Format or Initialize, because that erases the data on the drive.
u_disk.why: Windows can detect a drive but not show it in File Explorer until it has a drive letter.
u_disk.expect: The drive appears in File Explorer after you give it a letter.

u_done_disk.cause: The drive had no drive letter assigned.
u_done_disk.learn: File Explorer only lists drives that have a letter such as D: or E:. If the letter is missing, the drive exists but looks invisible.

u_restart.title: Restart the computer with the device unplugged
u_restart.do: Unplug the device. Use Start > Power > Restart. When Windows is back, plug the device in again.
u_restart.why: A restart reloads the USB controller and its drivers and clears temporary faults.
u_restart.expect: The computer restarts, and the device is detected when you plug it in again.

u_done_restart.cause: A temporary USB controller or driver glitch.
u_done_restart.learn: The USB controller is managed by drivers loaded in memory. A restart reloads them, which clears one-off faults.

u_devmgr.caution: Only uninstall the device named in this step and leave 'Delete the driver' unticked. Windows installs it again when you restart.
u_devmgr.title: Reinstall the USB driver
u_devmgr.do: Right-click Start and open Device Manager. Expand 'Universal Serial Bus controllers' (and 'Disk drives' for a drive). Right-click the device or any item with a yellow warning icon and choose 'Uninstall device' (leave 'delete the driver' unticked). Unplug the device, restart, and plug it in again.
u_devmgr.why: Windows installs a fresh copy of the driver at startup, which replaces a corrupted one.
u_devmgr.expect: Windows finds the device again and sets it up after the restart.
u_devmgr.technical: Removing the device entry forces Plug and Play to re-enumerate the device and reinstall its driver stack.

u_done_devmgr.learn: A driver is the software that lets Windows talk to a device. If it is damaged, working hardware can look dead until the driver is reinstalled.

u_power.title: Turn off USB power saving
u_power.do: In Device Manager, expand 'Universal Serial Bus controllers'. Double-click each 'USB Root Hub', open the Power Management tab, and untick 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'. Restart and test again.
u_power.why: Windows can switch USB ports off to save power, and some devices then disconnect or do not wake up.
u_power.expect: The device stays connected and no longer drops out.

u_done_power.cause: Windows power saving switched the USB port off.
u_done_power.learn: USB selective suspend lets Windows cut power to idle ports. Some devices do not wake up properly afterwards.

u_pro_device.reason: The device fails on another computer too, so the device or its cable is probably the problem and not your computer. If it is a drive with files you need, avoid plugging it in repeatedly and ask a technician about data recovery.

u_pro_usb.reason: The safe software checks are used up. The computer's USB ports or controller may need inspection. If the device is a drive with important files, avoid plugging it in repeatedly and ask a technician about data recovery.
